lessons.title: Foundations of full-stack architecture
learn: A client (browser or app) sends a request; a server processes it and sends a response.
Requests have a method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE), a path, headers and sometimes a body.
Resources have URLs (for example /users/1) and the HTTP method says the action.
One endpoint where the client asks for exactly the fields it needs.
lessons.practice: Prove you can read and make an HTTP exchange.

lessons.title: Frontend engineering (React and Next.js)
learn: The DOM is the live tree of page elements.
A component mounts, updates when its state or props change, and unmounts.
Keep state as local as possible.
lessons.practice: Build a counter and a shared cart count.

lessons.title: Backend engineering and databases
learn: Node runs JavaScript on the server.
An ORM maps database tables to code.
A relational database: tables, keys, joins, constraints and transactions.
A document database that stores JSON-like documents.

lessons.title: AI-assisted rapid development (vibe coding)
learn: Describing the app in words and letting an AI tool generate code.
Lovable and Bolt generate whole web apps from prompts.
lessons.practice: Build a feedback form with saved responses.

lessons.title: Deployment and DevOps
learn: Continuous integration runs tests on every change; continuous delivery deploys passing builds.

A container packages the app with its dependencies so it runs the same everywhere.
S3 stores files such as images.

lessons.title: WordPress core and custom theme development

WordPress picks the template file by page type: single.php for a post, page.php for a page, archive.php for lists, falling back to index.php.
Actions run your code at set points (add_action).
Keep wp-config.php outside public access where possible, use unique salts, disable file editing (DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT) and never commit credentials.
lessons.practice: Create a child theme with one filter.

lessons.title: Page builders and dynamic content
learn: Adds structured fields (price, date, image) to posts and pages.
Create content types such as Properties or Courses beyond Posts and Pages.

lessons.title: Automation integration (WordPress and n8n)
learn: Verify webhook signatures, return 200 quickly and make the flow safe to run twice.

lessons.title: Speed optimisation and hardening
learn: An object cache keeps repeated database results in memory.
A caching plugin: page cache, file minification and lazy loading.
Serves static files from nearby locations and adds protection.
Keep core, themes and plugins updated; limit login attempts; use two-factor sign-in; take backups and test restoring them.

1.name: Web Developer (vanilla JS and modern web standards)

lessons.title: HTML5 semantic structure and WCAG accessibility
learn: header, nav, main, section, article, footer give meaning to assistive tools and search engines.
Tab through the page, use a screen reader, and run an automated checker; automated tools catch only part of the issues.

lessons.title: Advanced CSS3
learn: One-dimensional layout: rows or columns with alignment and spacing.
Two-dimensional layout with rows and columns defined together.
Custom properties such as --brand store design values once.
Use transitions and keyframes on transform and opacity for smooth results; respect prefers-reduced-motion.
Utility classes written in the markup.

lessons.title: Modern JavaScript (ES6+)
learn: Writes promise code in a readable order.
fetch returns a promise; check response.ok because HTTP errors do not reject.
Synchronous code runs first, then microtasks (promises), then timers and other tasks.
import and export split code into files with clear dependencies.
lessons.practice: Predict the order, then run it.

lessons.title: Liquid templating engine
learn: Control flow such as {% if %} and {% for %}.
Data such as product, collection and cart, printed with {{ }}.
A JSON block in a section that gives merchants editable settings in the theme editor.

lessons.title: Custom sections and Shopify CLI workflows
learn: Reusable theme blocks with their own markup, settings and blocks.
Run the theme locally, push to a development theme and pull changes.
Keep the theme in Git so every change has a history.

lessons.title: Storefront API and headless commerce
learn: Read products and manage carts from your own front end using GraphQL.

lessons.title: Cross-platform engineering with React Native and Flutter
learn: JavaScript and React; renders native components.
Dart; draws its own interface with a consistent look across platforms.

lessons.title: Native device APIs
learn: Ask permission in context and handle refusal gracefully.
Register a device token and send through a push service; ask for consent and keep messages useful.
Store data locally and sync when online; decide how conflicts are resolved.

lessons.title: App store optimisation and deployment
learn: Title, subtitle, keywords, screenshots and ratings influence discovery.
Create the app, upload a signed bundle, complete the content and data-safety forms, test, then release.
Use an Apple Developer account, upload through App Store Connect, add privacy details and pass review.

lessons.title: Webflow box model, responsive layouts and Client-First naming
learn: Design for desktop then adjust breakpoints; test on real phones.
A naming system with consistent class names (for example section_ and u- utilities) so any teammate can edit the project.

lessons.title: Webflow CMS, dynamic filtering and custom code
learn: Fields, items and collection pages that share one template.
Filter lists by category or reference fields.
Add scripts in project settings or embeds, test them, and avoid loading unneeded libraries.

lessons.title: React hooks
learn: Local state; update with the setter, never by changing the value directly.
Side effects after render; list dependencies carefully and clean up.
Share values such as theme or user without passing props down every level.
Cache a computed value or a function between renders.

lessons.title: SSR vs SSG in Next.js
learn: Pages are built once at build time.
Pages are built on each request.

lessons.title: Cart logic, checkout, PCI-DSS and multi-currency
learn: Total = items, discounts, shipping and tax in a fixed order.
Validate stock and address, then create an order before payment is confirmed; confirm only after the payment provider says it succeeded.
The standard for protecting card data.
Show prices in the buyer's currency with a rate you can explain, round consistently and charge in the currency shown.

lessons.title: Payment gateway integration
learn: Each provides checkout pages, SDKs and webhooks.
Create an order on your server, open the provider's checkout, receive a webhook, verify its signature, then mark the order paid.
Use the provider's test keys and test cards; never test with real cards.

lessons.title: Next.js App Router, server actions, edge functions and middleware
learn: Folders define routes; layouts nest; server components run on the server by default.
Functions that run on the server and are called from forms or components.

lessons.title: Video production case studies and prompts

lessons.title: RAG-powered bots in Voiceflow, Botpress and Flowise
